title: Quantile-based headroom allocator for continuous batching and KV safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current headroom heuristics for continuous batching are overly conservative in many tenant/workload patterns, reserving memory for KV and activations that remains idle most of the time. This reduces effective GPU utilization and increases unit cost. Conversely, some bursty tenants still trigger OOMs or KV eviction cascades because static reserves do not reflect changing sequence-length distributions and active KV occupancy.

Proposal: Implement a quantile-based headroom allocator that computes per-GPU and per-tenant memory reserves from telemetry-derived distributions (sequence length, active KV bytes, batch arrival variance). The allocator will: compute a target memory reserve at a configurable quantile (e.g., 95th/99th) of observed working-set demand; convert the reserve into explicit budgets for weights (static), KV cache, and activations (dynamic); expose a fast path that the scheduler can use to accept/reject batch size increases or trigger smart offload to CPU/HBM; and provide a fallback grace policy that degrades concurrency before evicting KV.

Key ideas: predictive quantiles instead of fixed headroom; separate static weight accounting from dynamic KV/activation budgeting; per-tenant adjustments using Exponential Weighted Moving Quantiles to react to distributional shifts; integration with existing memory simulator to validate before rollout; observability surfaces for quantile drift and OOM near-misses.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator compares baseline headroom to quantile allocator across 30 representative tenant traces and shows >= 12% reduction in reserved memory without increase in OOM rate
Canary rollout (5% traffic) runs for 7 days with OOMs not exceeding baseline by more than 0.1% and 99th token latency within SLA
New metrics available in Console: headroom_quantile_target, reserved_kv_bytes, reserved_activation_bytes, quantile_drift_alert (boolean)
Scheduler integrates budget checks such that batch acceptance path uses the computed reserve; unit tests cover accept/reject and offload decisions
Documentation and runbook describing how to change quantile targets and how to respond to quantile_drift_alerts
tasks: Design and math spec for quantile estimator (EWMA-based approximate quantiles) and conversion to byte budgets
Extend memory simulator to run stochastic trials with quantile allocator and compare OOM/latency/cost
Implement allocator service API that returns per-GPU/per-tenant reserve vector (weights, kv, activations)
Integrate allocator into continuous batching admission/filter in runtime scheduler
Add telemetry: per-request sequence length, observed kv-resident-bytes, activation-peak-estimate
Create Console dashboard panels and alerts for quantile_drift and reserve-utilization (>80%, <30%)
Canary rollout plan and automated rollback criteria
Postmortem template and runbook for tune/rollback
comments: 2025-02-21 - PM review: Suggested adding a tenant-specific multiplier to avoid starving critical customers; agreed to expose multiplier as a tenant config in Dedicated/Private tiers.
2025-02-25 - Eng sync: Decided to use an EWMA-quantile approximation for low-memory footprint; exact t-digest was too heavyweight at runtime.
2025-02-28 - Design feedback: Dashboard should include small-multiple charts per-tenant showing distribution shifts, not just aggregates.
2025-03-02 - Security note: No new secrets; allocator uses only aggregated telemetry. Security review flagged that per-tenant labels must be scrubbed in shared telemetry exports.
2025-03-03 - Interim results from simulator: median reserved memory delta -18%, 95th OOM exposure unchanged in synthetic bursts; need more long-tail traces from production sampling.
